audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer calls this a 'Favoured matchup — difficulty 4/10, Mordekaiser carry threat 5/10' and gives Graves every phase at 6-8/10, while diff is already 'HARD', the packet win rate is 39.39% over 33 games, and the packet levelChart reads Skill / Mordekaiser x5 / Skill. The content layer's whys already describe Mordekaiser winning, so the full layer contradicts both the data and its own sibling layer.
audit.why: 39.39% Emerald+ win rate with a level chart Mordekaiser owns from Level 2 to first item is a losing lane, not a favoured one. Every full-layer phase side and rating, plus both difficulty strings, are inverted.
audit.corrected: Difficulty 7/10, Mordekaiser carry threat 8/10; phases Skill / Mordekaiser (L2-first item) / Skill, ratings 5,3,3,3,2,4,5 from the Graves side. Content win[0..6] flipped to match the packet chart as one atomic group.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why credits Graves' Level 6 to 'Collateral Damage adds an execute and a disengage knockback' and phases[5] claims the first item makes the point-blank pattern remove half bars. Level 6 is Mordekaiser's single strongest window, not Graves'.
audit.why: Realm of Death (R, 140/120/100s) removes the 1v1 from the map and steals a portion of Graves' stats. Graves' E dash and Smoke Screen relocate him inside the realm but cannot leave it, so his entire escape package is dead for the duration. The first-item window is real but only exists while R is on cooldown.
audit.corrected: Level 6 is Mordekaiser's spike; Graves' first item is the one fightable window and only on R's cooldown.
sources: enemyKit R Realm of Death, cd 140/120/100, range 650

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer never states the decisive interaction: Death's Grasp (E, 700 range, 16/14/12/10/8s) pulls Graves into Obliterate (Q, 675 range, 8/7/6/5/4s), which deals increased damage when it strikes a single enemy — so the pull manufactures the isolation bonus. Indestructible (W, 12/11/10/9/8s) then converts the damage of Graves' point-blank volley into a shield and a heal.
audit.why: Riot's own text: Q 'Damage is increased when hitting a single enemy'; E 'pulls all enemies in an area'; W 'stores damage he deals and takes to create a shield. He may consume the shield to heal.' The pull-into-isolated-Q-into-shield loop is why Graves' burst does not stick, and it is absent from every full-layer field.
audit.corrected: State the E-pull into isolated Obliterate, and that Indestructible recycles the point-blank volley into sustain. Graves' answer is spacing outside 700 units and anti-heal, not out-brawling.
sources: enemyKit Q/W/E Riot text and cooldowns
ownerKit P (4 bullets, cannot pass through units)

audit.why: Realm of Death at 140s rank 1 is correctly identified as the cooldown the lane runs on; only the fabricated 'fifteen-second invitation' in dosFull[2].d needed replacing with the real number.

audit.whatIsWrong: Multiple fields say Smoke Screen 'blinds' Mordekaiser.
audit.why: Riot's text for Graves' W is 'creating a cloud of smoke that reduces sight range' plus a brief slow — nearsight, not a blind. Calling it a blind implies his attacks miss, which is false, and the surrounding advice then leans on an effect that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Describe it as cutting his vision / zoning, not blinding.

audit.why: 39.39% over 33 games is the Emerald+ figure in the packet; no elo split appears anywhere in the text.

notes: Suspect name 'Use Smoke Screen' in wants.you[2] is a FALSE POSITIVE — Smoke Screen is Graves' real W name per the kit; the actual error in that line was calling it a blind. The full layer for this matchup was written as if Graves wins (every phase Graves, 'Favoured matchup', 4/10) while diff was already 'HARD', the packet reads 39.39% over 33 games, and the content layer's whys correctly describe Mordekaiser winning — the two layers were describing opposite lanes. All seven phase side/rating flips are proposed together as one atomic level-chart group. Kit flag caution: the brief's derived flags put 'grounding: shuts off enemy dashes' on Mordekaiser's Q (Obliterate); Riot's own description for that ability says only 'smashes the ground with his mace dealing damage to each enemy struck. Damage is increased when hitting a single enemy' — no grounding. Per the trust-the-description rule I did not assert any grounding effect anywhere in this matchup, so no advice depends on it.
